question: Who headed the 1915 committee to examine the co-operative movement in India?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Sir Edward Maclagan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Edward Maclagan** was an important figure in the history of cooperative movements in India.
 
• He headed the **1915 Committee**, which was formed to examine the **cooperative movement** in India.
 
• The committee was tasked with studying the functioning and **impact of cooperative societies** and their role in the development of rural areas.
 
• The findings of the committee emphasized the importance of **cooperatives** as a tool for **economic and social upliftment** in the country.
 
• It laid the foundation for further reforms and development in the cooperative sector, including the introduction of the **Cooperative Societies Act**.
 
• The committee recommended measures to improve the **efficiency** and expand the reach of cooperative societies in India.
 
• Cooperative movements were seen as vital for addressing issues like **rural credit shortages** and promoting **self-reliance** among farmers and rural communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Curzon**__

 __
 
• **Lord Curzon** was a British statesman who served as the **Viceroy of India** from 1899 to 1905.
 
• He is known for his controversial decision to **partition Bengal** in 1905, which led to widespread protests and the eventual reversal of the partition in 1911.
 
• He played a key role in the establishment of the **Archaeological Survey of India** to preserve historical monuments.
 
 
 
• **Lord Irwin**__
 __
 
• **Lord Irwin**, also known as **Edward Wood**, served as the Viceroy of India from 1926 to 1931.
 
• He is notable for signing the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** in 1931, which marked a crucial moment in India’s struggle for independence.
 
• His tenure was marked by the **Civil Disobedience Movement** led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
 
 
• **Sir John Simon**__
 
 
• **Sir John Simon** was a British politician and head of the **Simon Commission**, which arrived in India in 1928.
 
• The commission was tasked with reviewing the **constitutional reforms** in India but faced widespread opposition due to the absence of Indian representation.
 
• The protests against the Simon Commission were a significant event in India’s freedom struggle, leading to the demand for **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence).
